i want to write a review on the inpatient dining "expressly for you." there is a menu that you can order what you want. there are specific times that you must be followed in ensure your meal order is placed in time. i have ordered many things from the menu, overall, i think they try to be to fancy and offer too many complex meal options. when i am sick, i prefer to eat very simple things without a ton of spice or flavor. this may just be me, but here are some of my thoughts on things i have ordered. 

scrambled eggs: the first time i ordered scrambled eggs they arrived with onions and peppers. this was not expected. the next time i ordered, i specified that i wanted scrambled eggs plain without onions or peppers. this time it arrived with a garnish orange slice that spread orange juice on my eggs and rendering them inedible. if you just want eggs, order without garnish! 

oatmeal: this is a solid basic. it is pretty bland by itself, but would highly recommend adding banana slices and a packet of cream cheese. 

pimento cheese plate: this is a generous scoop of pimento cheese and served with fresh veggies and pita. i wasn't feeling up to eating much, but what i did eat was great! 

cheeseburger and fries: one night i didn't get a dinner order placed, so they brought me a late tray option. it was a freshly made burger and fries. i may have just been super hungry, but this was amazing!! 

chicken salad sandwich: this was okay. the chicken salad had too much mayo for my taste, but not bad. 

chicken tenders: there was a lot of breading, but easy to peel off.

baked potato: good simple option and can order shredded cheese and sour cream on the side.

clear liquid diet: i'm not sure much can be done to make this better, but this is rough! the tray comes with broth (i sampled vegetable, chicken, and beef), jello, juice, or flavored water. the broth was always luke warm and never appealing, but this is likely a result of how i was feeling. pro tip:  the floors stock popsicles, so that is a great alternative/supplement to the tray. 

if you miss ordering off the menu or get to your room late the floors stock some boxed meals. one night my diet was advanced from clears to regular diet late and i wanted solid food. they brought me a turkey sandwich boxed lunch. i ate the turkey (not then bread) a standard basic turkey sandwich which is a good option when the cafeteria is closed. 

things i wish were on the menu: greek yogurt. they have sugary yogurt, but i really wish there was greek yogurt, low fat string cheese sticks, plain tuna without being in tuna salad, or other high protein simple options. 

the people that take your order on the phone are really helpful and willing to get you want you want!

warning.  good samaritan is quick to send outstanding balances to a collection agency, with little to no effort in collecting outstanding balances beforehand. 

my 90 year-old mother, with limited english and fixed income/resources, had a pre-scheduled outpatient cataract surgery at good samaritan hospital late 2019. although it is common best practice in scheduled surgeries, good samaritan apparently did not collect the $125 co-pay during the pre-registration process. 

with little to no effort to collect the co-pay, good samaritan sent the account to a collections agency. as i've read in other yelp reviews, that may be their standard practice for processing accounts receivables, rather than expending minimal effort in working with patients on outstanding balances. they make up for their short-comings in their accounts receivable process with aggressive action, displaying little compassion, even during a pandemic. 

fortunately for my elderly mother, a bad credit rating will not affect her life, but if you are concerned with maintaining a good credit rating, i strongly recommend choosing another hospital that will make a minimal effort in collecting outstanding balances before sending your account to a collections agency. it could have a severe, negative impact on your credit rating.

mountainview hospital has adequate supplies of ppe. the problem is that the hospital is not giving those supplies to the nurses who are currently on the front lines working with covid-19+ patients on a daily basis. worse even, they are not allowing nurses to protect themselves when they have the ability to do so. this is not in alignment with what you say is the hospital's top priority of "protecting your patients, clinicians, nurses and colleagues so you can best serve our communities..." in fact, it seems quite the opposite, it would almost appear as though your policies are directly intended to put our patients, clinicians, nurses and colleagues at a greater risk.

here are the facts about what mountainview hospital is doing at this moment:

* a nurse is only given an n95 rated respirator if they are working directly with a covid-19+ patient that is undergoing aerosol treatments while the nurse providing care to this patient.
* a nurses is only allowed to wear a surgical mask around covid-19+ patients who are not undergoing aerosol treatments as well as all others that are presumed to have covid-19 but are waiting the 3-5 days it takes for test results to come back. 
* nurses who bring in their own n95 or kn95 rated respirators are required to remove them and replace them with the hospital supplied surgical mask.
* doctors seem to have a different set of rules that apply to them as doctors have been observed wearing n95 respirator brought in from home under their surgical masks without recourse. however, your nurses have been told if they attempt to wear an n95 or kn95 respirator, even under their surgical masks, they will be required to leave the hospital and not be allowed to return until they submit to the hospital's ludicrous policies. 

remember, our nurses and doctors live at home with their families and loved ones. if they catch this nasty virus, they bring it home to us as well. your hospital's policies are a possible death sentence to not only your own staff but to our entire community!

what i would like to understand is what is the harm in allowing a nurse to wear an n95 or kn95 mask which they bring in themselves and is very likely to provide much more protection than the hospital supplied surgical mask which has been cited even by the cdc to be inadequate protection against covid-19? our nurses and doctors are the most at-risk people in our community. we already have communities around the world where 20-30 percent of health-care professionals in a region have become infected with the virus. what is the hospital's thinking here in requiring better protection to be removed?

doc_text: ok let me start off by saying i've been to many psych wards in seattle and at first site or intake may be a little rough around the edges i was in 3w which is a pretty hectic place but there was gems within this unit including the loving staff that actually care.  i would like to point out that i wasnt in a good shape so my perception may be different from today.  looking back i'd like to say that my overall experience on 3w was rough its loud and there are many sick ppl so its not a hilton hotel so the expectation should be different right, well being hospitalized during corona virus makes everything 100% worse no going outside for one month!
